doc.title: Robert Glasper interviewed by Greg Thomas, Clinton, New York, February 20, 2016

title: Where music is going
summary: He does not know, but says good music comes in waves while bad music is always present.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Where do you see music in the next ten years, from dealing with the whole fusion thing that we have going on now, and mixing in the whole like neo-soul, Gospel feel and everything. Where do you see it going?

I don’t know. Because there’s two waves going on. There’s one side, it’s like what the hell are you doing in music? And then there’s the other side whereas like that’s awesome. And they’re both doing this. And I don’t know. I have no idea. I wish I knew the answer to that but I don’t know. I hope people keep, like I said there’s always waves of great organic music. And there’s always bad music. Bad music never goes in waves. It’s just there. It’s like the good shit’s wavy and the bad music’s just there. So I’m hoping the good music will stop being as wavy. Or you know the good music’s always been there, it’s just not as accessible as other music. It’s not in your face. Not as obvious. You’ve got to dig for it. Versus bad music, it’s in your face. When you get in a cab it’s going to be there. You know. You know you could sing a song that you hate because of that. Because they get so much marketing for these bad songs.
